title: Sheinbaum Responds to Trump: “Mexico Is Not and Will Not Be a Colony”
author: Fernanda Monroy
content:
_This article by[Fernanda
Monroy](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/fermonroy/) originally appeared in
the [September 7, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/sheinbaum-responde-a-
trump-mexico-no-es-ni-sera-colonia/), Mexico's leading investigative
journalism magazine._

**Mexico "is not and will not be a colony or protectorate of any foreign
country,"** declared **President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo** , after U.S.
President **Donald Trump** circulated on social media a map in which **Mexico,
Canada, Greenland,** and other territories appear covered with **elements of
the United States flag.**

Amid the month of the homeland, the president responded to the post through
her X account and reaffirmed national sovereignty: "In the month of the
homeland, we reaffirm that Mexico is not and will not be a colony or
protectorate of any foreign country."

> We are proudly a free, independent, and sovereign country.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

> [Post by @Claudiashein on
> X](https://twitter.com/Claudiashein/status/2096995458958712907)

President Trump's post adds to a series of messages and decisions related to
the geographic representation of territories and bodies of water in North
America.

Just a day earlier, Trump had circulated on his Truth Social network an image
of the state of New Mexico in which the word "Mexico" appeared crossed out and
replaced with "America." In addition, the president has also publicly proposed
calling the state "New America," although the U.S. federal government does not
have the authority to unilaterally change a state's official name.

![Map circulated by Trump showing North American territories under U.S. flag
elements](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/02-map.png)Image: Contralínea

The proposal drew rejection from New Mexico authorities. Governor **Michelle
Lujan Grisham** maintained that the state's name **" is not up for debate"**
and recalled that **its name has existed since before the creation of the
United States.**

Likewise, President Claudia Sheinbaum's response comes just days after the
**General Assembly of the United Nations (UN)** approved a resolution to
**promote cartographic representations that more accurately reflect the size
of the continents**.

The document, promoted by Togo and other African countries, received **164
votes in favor** , one against—that of the United States—and six abstentions.
The resolution promotes the **use of projections such as Equal Earth** , which
represent the surface of landmasses more proportionally and **question the
widespread use of the Mercator projection.**

The UN's proposal calls for governments, international organizations,
educational institutions, and other actors to use representations that make it
possible to more faithfully appreciate the relative dimensions of territories.

The Mercator projection, created in the 16th century to facilitate navigation,
distorts the size of surfaces as latitude increases. As a result, northern
territories appear visually much larger than they actually are. Greenland, for
example, can appear comparable in size to Africa on this type of map, even
though the African continent has a surface area roughly 14 times larger.

During the discussion at the United Nations, **Togo 's Minister of Foreign
Affairs, Robert Dussey**, argued that maps are not merely technical tools, but
representations that influence the way societies understand the world. **"
Maps shape our understanding of the world."**

The debate over cartographic representation thus took on a political and
cultural dimension: while the initiative promoted by African countries seeks
to reduce a historical distortion in the way territorial dimensions are
represented, the image circulated by Trump places territories belonging to
other countries under U.S. symbols.

The post about Mexico is also part of a policy of changing geographic names
promoted by Trump since the start of his second term.

In January 2025, the president signed an executive order for the U.S.
government to use the name "**Gulf of America** " to refer to the **Gulf of
Mexico**. The measure has effects within the U.S. government and does not by
itself change the body of water's international designation.

More recently, on **August 27, 2026** , Trump **signed another executive order
for the U.S. government to use "Lake America" instead of Lake Ontario** in its
official references. The document instructed the Department of the Interior
and the U.S. Board on Geographic Names to carry out the corresponding actions
within the federal geographic names system.

Added to this series of actions is now the proposal to rename **New Mexico**
as **" New America,"** as well as the image circulated in which Mexico and
Canada appear under the U.S. flag.

The name of New Mexico, moreover, has a history that predates the creation of
the United States and of independent Mexico. The designation began to be used
during the Spanish colonial period to identify territories located north of
New Spain and remained after Mexican independence and the territory's
incorporation into the United States.

President Sheinbaum's response comes as her government maintains, as one of
its main foreign-policy matters, the relationship with the United States, in
which it has emphasized binational cooperation without accepting a
relationship of subordination.
